blocks.x: Computer-vision drive-thru intelligence, service time down 14 seconds and order accuracy up 6 points at peak

A quick-service restaurant group: Retail chains feel decision gaps in margin per store, visible in the weekly numbers. The Achala program started with the pricing and availability flow —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline quarter timed the peak: 289-second average service time at lunch rush, 91% order accuracy with errors concentrated in customization-heavy orders, and crew scheduling built on averages that peaked differently every site.
Timer data existed per lane but connected to nothing: no weather, no staffing, no menu mix. The ops team argued about the timer without ever seeing what moved it.

We built the drive-thru twin: lane cameras timing each stage with consent-clear analytics, service stages decomposed, order, pay, handoff, so the slow stage is a fact not a feeling, forecast models joining menu mix, weather and staffing to stage times, and the crew schedule adapting per site to its own shape. The timer finally told the truth and got to act on it.
